steps.text: Whisk together 1 cup plus 2 tablespoons mayonnaise with sugar, salt, onion powder, ground mustard, and paprika until smooth.
Stir in ketchup, vinegar, and Worcestershire sauce until well blended.
Cover and refrigerate until chilled, about 30 minutes. Store covered in the refrigerator.

raw_recipe.headline: Idaho Fry Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This mayonnaise-based fry sauce with tangy seasoning is just what you need to jazz up your french fries. Made with easy ingredients you already have.
raw_recipe.name: Idaho Fry Sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Whisk together 1 cup plus 2 tablespoons mayonnaise with sugar, salt, onion powder, ground mustard, and paprika until smooth.
Stir in ketchup, vinegar, and Worcestershire sauce until well blended.
Cover and refrigerate until chilled, about 30 minutes. Store covered in the refrigerator.

review.reviewBody: This is so good and it is also quick to make. I used the calculate button to change it to 8 servings and it made a 1/2 cup as the full recipe is 2 cups. I used Kraft mayo with olive oil and it worked great. Such a nice change over plain ketchup. We dipped fries and onion rings in it. Only problem with this dip is that now I might eat too many fries!

Giving it a 4 since it is much better than ketchup and mayo but I needed more spice myself. Made as directed but cut the sugar in half (enough in the ketchup). After using it a bit I then added more onion powder, paprika, salt and dry mustard but really looking for more of a kick. I did enjoy it though but next time, I think I'll try doubling the seasonings or add some hot sauce. ******Made a second time, doubled all the seasonings, but kept the mayo and ketchup the same. This is what I was looking for, very nice.
An easier method is 1 cup mayo stirred with 1 tb pickle juice till smooth, add 1 cup ketchup, stir till smooth. Done.

I came across this recipe a few years ago and I made it one evening to see if the grandkids would like it. And it was an overwhelming success, now I have to keep the fridge stocked at all times.When I make it I exchange the salt for garlic salt. Since I love to use garlic for flavoring when I cook, it was a no brainer to use garlic salt to replace regular salt. I read some comments on this thread and there were several that said it was too sweet. Since I have to watch my sugar intake, I cut back on the sugar that I add but because I add less sugar, I had to decrease the vinegar too. If y'all haven't made this sauce before, then what are you waiting for? Hop to it and I can guarantee that u'll love it. It's not just for fries, it's good on hamburgers and chicken strips and just about whatever food that you can dip.

This is a quick dipping sauce to make and tastes good. I made it exactly as the recipe stated. Next time though, I will omit the sugar as the first batch was way too sweet. Ketchup has a lot of sugar already in it, so I don't see any reason to add more. Other than that, thank you for this recipe.

Per other comments, we reduced the amount of sugar and used 1/4 of what was called for but the red wine vinegar is overpowering even at 1.5 tbsp (recipe calls for 2 tbsp). I grew up in North Idaho eating Zip's fry sauce and several local variations of the mythical dip. I think this is on the right track, but basically inedible due to the very strong red wine vinegar flavor. Hard to believe this isn't repeated by every review... but then again, I might be more familiar with this PNW classic.

Very good Fry Sauce, so much better than Ketchup and Mayo. I did reduce the amount of sugar by 1/2, I'm not sure that you really need any sugar. I've tasted a lot of different fry sauces and I think that this one is the best, hands down!!!!

Like most fry sauces, this one was missing a little something. Fry sauces typically tend to be a little too sweet and tasting of mostly mayo with no savory present . To make this a five star recipe for my family and I, I added 1 - 1 1/2 Tbs of barbecue sauce to the original recipe as written. I would lean toward a mesquite or hickory BBQ sauce. Be careful not to add too much BBQ sauce otherwise it starts tasting like campfire sauce and not a fry sauce.
I added a couple of teaspoons of dill pickle juice!!
I love this recipe. I add some horseradish to give it a little zing!

Idaho native here, been eating fry sauce for about 50 years now, since I could eat fries as a toddler.

This is probably the best fry sauce I've had in a long long time. Made it just as directed and then made it again to have a spare bottle in the fridge.

2nd bottle I added a bit of garlic for fun.

Thank you for this amazing recipe!
Other than cutting it in half, I made this recipe exactly as written, and it is PERFECT!
Totally forgot about this wonderful memory from travelling in Utah!
Also is great as a dipping sauce for Chicken tenders or on Spicy Chicken sandwiches.. Try It!

I've made this my whole life (50 years). Mine is more simple though. 4 parts mayo, 2 parts ketchup, 1 part yellow mustard. I didn't find out about the Idaho sauce until 10 years ago. I may try adding the dash of sugar. I also put this on everything like hamburgers and hot dogs.

Yummmm. Really good. Creamy and rich with flavor. This is a little bit sweet, a little tangy, and a whole lotta good. It's reminiscent of ketchup, yet it's not ketchup. This took no time to make and the hardest part was waiting on it to sit in the fridge to let the flavors develop.

This sauce is awesome! I take it to all the restaurants with me now. I have had several customers, while eating, ask me about the sauce and what is in it. I now carry a copy of the recipe with me. LOL. Thanks for sharing.
Very good!! Made our air fryer french fries extra special!

Yep, absolutely nailed it. When I moved to Moscow, ID 15 years ago I was introduced to fry sauce. I thought it was weird at first but now it’s a staple; I just couldn’t figure out the right recipe to make it taste authentic. I’ve heard “just mix mayo, ketchup, and Johnny salt.” Nope. I think it’s the sugar and red wine vinegar that makes it. I just whipped up a small bowl and winged the measurements. Thank you!

OMG!!! Wish I could give this 10 stars! Just made this for the first time tonight. Absolutely to die for. I could just about "drink" this stuff up. No more mixing just ketchup and mayo any more. Thank you for sharing a true gem. Shared half with a neighbor who also loved it.
